src/infrastructure/composition/buildControllers.ts: `export function buildControllers(): Controllers` is the only composition root. It creates `const ids = new UuidIdGenerator()` once and passes it to CreateUserUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase and CreateTaskUseCase.

src/infrastructure/composition/buildControllers.ts: the repositories (InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository) and TaskAssignmentService are each created once and shared, so no wiring is duplicated.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: `createApp(buildControllers()).listen(port, ...)` hands all wiring to the composition root and only handles port config and startup.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files share one infrastructure concern: they provide concrete adapters and wire them together to start the app. UuidIdGenerator is a concrete adapter that implements the domain IdGenerator port. buildControllers is the only composition root. It creates the adapters once, passes them through constructors to the use cases and controllers, and returns the Controllers type from http/createApp. server.ts is a thin entry point that reads the port and hands buildControllers() to createApp. No rule or invariant is duplicated: ID generation, wiring and server startup each live in exactly one file. None of the files bypasses the module's abstractions: controllers get their use cases through constructor injection, and server.ts uses the composition root rather than building dependencies itself. Import direction is out of scope.
